subtopic: Graph break and recompile log diagnosis
learningObjective: Diagnose torch.compile graph breaks and recompiles from the TORCH_LOGS='+dynamo,recompiles' output and identify remediation strategies.
stem: The following TORCH_LOGS output was captured for a torch.compile'd function processing a variable-length batch. Which conclusions are correct? (Select all that apply.)
profileData:
TORCH_LOGS='+dynamo,recompiles' output for f(x, mask):

[0] torch._dynamo.convert_frame: Recompiling function f (call 1) — new signature
[0] torch._dynamo.symbolic_convert: graph break on `if mask.any():` — data-dependent branch
[0] torch._inductor: compiled subgraph #0 (before break), #1 (after break)

[1] torch._dynamo.convert_frame: Recompiling function f (call 2) — guard failure: tensor 'x' size changed 128 → 256
[1] torch._inductor: recompile of #0 and #1

[2] torch._dynamo.convert_frame: Recompiling function f (call 3) — guard failure: tensor 'x' size changed 256 → 128
[2] torch._inductor: cache hit on #0 (size 128 already compiled), cache hit on #1

options.text: The 'cache hit' at call 3 shows that torch.compile keeps compiled subgraphs indexed by (shape, dtype) guard set — bouncing between two sizes stops paying compile cost after both have been seen once, but each still uses shape-specific code.

Replacing `if mask.any():` with `torch.where(mask, x, 0)` — an eager pattern that avoids the graph break — would still cause the same recompiles because guard failures on tensor shapes are unrelated to control flow.

The `if mask.any():` triggers a graph break because it is a data-dependent Python control flow; the compiled region is split into two subgraphs (#0 before and #1 after) with eager execution of the branch decision itself in between.

The recompile at call 2 is due to a shape guard failure (128 → 256); enabling dynamic shapes for `x` (`torch._dynamo.mark_dynamic(x, 0)`) would avoid the recompile by generating a shape-generic compiled graph that handles both sizes.

explanation: C: data-dependent Python control flow forces a graph break, splitting compilation into subgraphs #0 and #1. D: enabling dynamic shape via `mark_dynamic` avoids per-shape recompiles by generating one shape-generic compiled graph. A: torch.compile keeps compiled subgraphs indexed by shape/dtype guards, so bouncing between two known sizes stops paying compile cost after both have been seen (the log shows 'cache hit on #0' at call 3). B is wrong because rewriting `if mask.any():` to `torch.where` removes the graph break (unlocking fusion across the branch); that is a real, separate benefit from what shape guards do, so the claim that 'rewriting has no effect on compile behavior' conflates the two orthogonal mechanisms.

optionExplanations.A: Correct: cache-indexed compiles stabilize after all shapes seen.
optionExplanations.B: Wrong: the rewrite eliminates the graph break (unlocking fusion across the branch); the claim that 'rewriting has no effect' conflates two orthogonal mechanisms.

assumptions: cache_size_limit is not being exceeded by the two shapes in the log.
nonImplications: Does not imply mark_dynamic has zero cost; the compiled shape-generic kernel can be slower per iteration.
Does not imply graph breaks are always bad; some are unavoidable and negligible.

distractorRationales.B: Conflates shape guard with graph break impact.
